newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish high real rates to rise debt costs - Kolodko.
newsitem.headline: Polish high real rates to rise debt costs - Kolodko.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Friday the central bank's plan to let real interest rates rise would increase costs of public debt servicing but that he had no qualms about such policy.

"When inflation falls and nominal rates remain unchanged and if credit becames more expensive...it is obvious that this has a direct impact on public debt servicing costs and is a burden for taxpayers," Kolodko told a news briefing.

"We adjust our actions to decisions that do not depend on us. For me, NBP rates are an independent factor," he said on his arrival from the annual conference of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
But asked if he approved or dispproved of the NBP plans he said: "The NBP policy serves the Polish economy well."

The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, said on Thursday that it wanted real interest rates to rise to keep credit action in check and protect the balance of payments from a potential imports boom.

The rise would be achieved by keeping the key discount and lombard rates fixed at the current level of 22 and 25 percent respectively despite falling inflation or by making sure they were reduced more slowly than inflation.
NBP deputy president Witold Kozinski said that the move was aimed at controlling a recent boom in credit action.
Consumer credit grew 64.5 percent since the start of the year, against corporate credit growth of 19.5 percent in that period and a deposits growth of 31.0 percent and 7.8 percent respectively.

But Kolodko said that the credit expansion was not a sign that the economy was overheating, especially that the year-on-year inflation was estimated to come down to 18.9 percent in September from 20.5 percent in August.

"Companies make money and will make more money, they have a great potential to be competitive and this is the basis for the success of the Polish economy and not for an overheating resulting from inappropriate financial instruments," he said.

He confirmed his policy would be aimed at maintaining growth at the current level of more than five percent annually and at cuurbing inflation to 13 percent in December next year from 21.6 percent last year.
Kolodko said he would resist likely pressure for more spending during coming government and parliamentary debates on the 1997 national budget.

The Polish Peasant Party (PSL), the smaller partner in the ruling leftist coalition, has said it would demand increased spending for education and health care system, recently experiencing repeated protests and pay rise demands.

The finance ministry's budget draft, which proposes a cut in deficit to 2.7 percent of gross domestic product next year from 2.8 percent planned for 1996, is due to be submitted to the government on October 10. It has to be submitted to parliament before October 31.
